dossier.purpose: OpenBao is a community-run fork of HashiCorp Vault (publiccode.yml:24-25), governed as 'OpenBao, a Series of LF Projects, LLC' (CHARTER.md:8) and licensed MPL-2.0 (LICENSE:3). It ships as one Go binary, `bao` (server, CLI, agent, proxy), that stores, generates on demand, encrypts, leases and revokes secrets, certificates and keys behind an authenticated, ACL-gated, audited HTTP API (README.md:33-72). It is a secrets manager. It has no secret-scanning feature (staged changes, history or directories) and no feature that verifies found credentials against provider APIs. The repository's own hooks and CI use neither kind of tool (see claim_checks and risks).

claims.claim: OpenBao is 'a software solution to manage, store, and distribute sensitive data including secrets, certificates, and keys'. The community 'intends to provide this software under an OSI-approved open-source license', led under open-governance principles.

Problem statement: knowing who accesses which secrets is hard, and 'adding on key rolling, secure storage, and detailed audit logs is almost impossible without a custom solution. This is where OpenBao steps in.'
Secure Secret Storage: arbitrary key/value secrets are encrypted before being written to persistent storage; 'OpenBao can write to disk, PostgreSQL, and more.'
Dynamic Secrets: generated on demand 'for some systems, such as AWS or SQL databases' (example: an AWS keypair for an S3 bucket) and automatically revoked when the lease ends.
Data Encryption: OpenBao can encrypt and decrypt data without storing it.
Leasing and Renewal: every secret has a lease and is revoked automatically at the end of it; clients renew via built-in renew APIs.
Revocation: single secrets or a tree of secrets (all read by a user, or all of a type) can be revoked.
Security issues must be reported privately to openbao-security@lists.openssf.org.
OpenSSF Scorecard and OpenSSF Best Practices badges are shown.
Docs are on the website (openbao.org/docs). The README itself only documents building from source ('go build -o bin/bao .') and a dev server ('go run . server -dev'); it has no install section.
The Go toolchain version used in CI and releases is pinned in .go-version.
The repo also houses the docs website (website/) and the web UI (ui/).
The repo publishes two importable libraries, github.com/openbao/openbao/api/v2 and github.com/openbao/openbao/sdk/v2. Importing the root module is 'NOT, and has NEVER been' a supported use.
Contributors must read CONTRIBUTING.md first or the PR will likely be rejected.

install.command: Add /etc/apt/sources.list.d/openbao.sources (Types: deb; URIs: https://pkgs.openbao.org/deb/; Suites: stable; Components: main; Signed-By: <openbao-gpg-pub-20240618.asc>), then: sudo apt update && sudo apt install openbao

dnf install -y epel-release   then   dnf install -y openbao   (alternative: add /etc/yum.repos.d/openbao.repo with baseurl https://pkgs.openbao.org/rpm/$basearch, then sudo yum install -y openbao; downloads.tsx:270-284). Arch Linux: pacman -Sy openbao (install.mdx:44-48).
docker pull ghcr.io/openbao/openbao:<version>   (same names on quay.io and docker.io; variants openbao-ubi and openbao-distroless)

install.method: Precompiled binary archive (GitHub release) with checksum verification
install.command: wget "https://github.com/openbao/openbao/releases/download/v$VERSION/$RELEASE" with RELEASE="openbao_${VERSION}_${PLATFORM}.tar.gz", plus checksums.txt; then: sha256sum --ignore-missing --check checksums.txt. Docs say the package is a zip (install.mdx:86-87), but non-Windows archives are .tar.gz (scripts/release/archive.sh:28-31).
mkdir -p bin && go build -o bin/bao .   (docs variant: make bootstrap && make dev)

integrations.cli: Yes - the `bao` binary (main.go:12-14). About 127 subcommands are registered in internal/command/commands.go (server, agent, proxy, operator, kv, pki, transit, token, login, policy, audit, plugin...). Docs: website/content/docs/commands/index.mdx. The CLI caches its token via a token helper at ~/.vault-token or BAO_TOKEN_PATH (website/content/docs/commands/index.mdx:261-272; internal/command/token/helper_internal.go:26-35). BAO_* env vars fall back to the legacy VAULT_* names (api/env.go:22-34), and the Alpine/UBI images symlink `vault` to `bao` (Dockerfile:32,81).
integrations.mcp: none found - no MCP server in code or docs. The only mention is a hypothetical optional UI plugin ('An AI agent plugin with MCP command suggestions') in an RFC (website/content/community/rfcs/web-ui-modernization.mdx:77).
integrations.sdk_or_api: Yes - HTTP API v1 (website/content/docs/api/index.mdx:6-14) with a warning that backwards compatibility is not yet promised (index.mdx:16-23). OpenAPI document served at /sys/internal/specs/openapi (website/content/docs/api/system/internal-specs-openapi.mdx:9). Official Go client github.com/openbao/openbao/api/v2 (website/content/docs/api/libraries.mdx:28-34; api/README.md:4) plus api/auth/{approle,jwt,kubernetes,ldap,userpass} helper modules (Makefile:284-299), and the plugin SDK github.com/openbao/openbao/sdk/v2 (sdk/go.mod:1). The docs state Vault client libraries should also work (libraries.mdx:15-20). `bao agent` and `bao proxy` daemons cover auto-auth, token sinks and API proxying (internal/command/agent.go, proxy.go).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: none found - no CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .codex/, .cursor/, .mcp.json or skill files (repo-wide glob). The project's contribution policy tells contributors to disable generative AI agents, naming Claude Code (CONTRIBUTING.md:38-54; website/content/community/contributing/index.mdx:15-17). The PR template asks contributors to certify no generative-AI use (.github/pull_request_template.md:33-35), and AI-generated issues or security reports may be closed (CONTRIBUTING.md:109-116).

readme.telemetry_and_network: Telemetry/phone-home: none found. A repo-wide search of Go code, docs and scripts for usage-reporting, update-check, census and Sentry patterns found nothing. getsentry/sentry-go appears only as an indirect go.mod dependency (go.mod:219) and no Go file imports it. The web UI sets Scarf telemetry off (ui/package.json:229-231). Metrics are local-first: an in-memory sink is always created (internal/helper/configutil/telemetry.go:264), and external sinks (Prometheus, statsite, statsd, Circonus, DogStatsD, Stackdriver) exist only when the operator configures them (telemetry.go:283-380; website/content/docs/configuration/telemetry.mdx:10-18). The OpenTelemetry SDK is imported only under internal/vault/diagnose for `bao operator diagnose` spans (internal/vault/diagnose/helpers.go:14-18). Opt-in outbound fetches: OCI plugin auto-download is off by default (plugin_auto_download false, website/content/docs/configuration/index.mdx:151-152; internal/command/server.go:2436-2446), while plugin_auto_register defaults true (index.mdx:154; internal/command/server/config.go:1093-1101); Raft auto_join uses go-discover provider lookups only when configured (go.mod:51; CHANGELOG.md:21). Required services/accounts: no project account or API key is needed by the documented install/run steps. The server needs a storage backend chosen by the operator (local raft/pebbledb, or external PostgreSQL; internal/command/commands.go:145-151), listens on 8200 (dev default 127.0.0.1:8200, website/content/docs/commands/server.mdx:113-115; packaged config binds 0.0.0.0:8200 with TLS cert files, .release/linux/package/etc/openbao/openbao.hcl:17-21) and uses 8201 for cluster traffic (.release/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:33-35). Clients default to https://127.0.0.1:8200 and BAO_ADDR (api/client.go:34,403). Auth methods and auto-unseal call whatever IdP/KMS the operator configures (internal/helper/builtinplugins/registry.go:58-65). Startup logs the proxy environment (http_proxy, https_proxy, no_proxy) with URL credentials redacted (internal/command/server.go:677-700), although the CLI docs say 'All environment variables available to the OpenBao process will be logged during startup' (website/content/docs/commands/index.mdx:279-280). Project-side infrastructure that users do not need: GitHub Actions, ghcr.io/quay.io/docker.io, an S3 bucket behind pkgs.openbao.org (.github/workflows/release-packages.yml:30-34) and a Codeberg mirror (.github/workflows/mirror.yml:33-34).

entry_points.what: Run() CLI dispatcher plus global flag and env handling (main.go:145)
Registers all CLI subcommands (about 127 factories) and the audit, physical and service-registration backend maps (commands.go:125-158,180)
`bao server`: config load, OCI plugin download (:1037), telemetry setup (:1048), storage setup (:710), -dev mode
`bao agent` (auto-auth, token sinks, templating); `bao proxy` is in internal/command/proxy.go
Go HTTP API client; reads BAO_ADDR / BAO_TOKEN (client.go:34,821); default address https://127.0.0.1:8200 (client.go:403)
Release build: go build -tags=ui with version ldflags (build.sh:31)

Three image targets (default Alpine, ubi, distroless); default CMD is `server -dev -dev-no-store-token`, which the file says is not for production (Dockerfile:56-58); entrypoint script .release/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh

code.architecture: Single Go module github.com/openbao/openbao/v2 (go.mod:1) producing `bao` (main.go -> internal/command). Layers: CLI/daemon commands (internal/command/: server, agent, proxy, operator, kv, pki, token...) -> HTTP handler (internal/http/; the web UI built from ui/ is embedded from internal/http/web_ui when built with -tags=ui, website/content/community/contributing/packaging.mdx:42,63-65) -> Core (internal/vault/): AES-GCM encryption barrier (internal/vault/barrier/aes_gcm.go:999-1013), token store (token_store.go), lease/expiration manager (expiration.go), audit (audit.go), ACL policy (internal/vault/policy/), request router (internal/vault/routing/), namespaces, identity. The server starts sealed; Shamir shares (default 5, threshold 3) or auto-unseal plugins are used (website/content/docs/internals/security.mdx:173-185). Storage backends: internal/physical/{raft,postgresql,pebbledb,inmem}, with sdk/physical/{file,inmem} left as packages (the `file` backend was removed from the server in 2.7.0, website/content/community/release-notes/2-7-0.mdx:77). Built-in plugins are registered in internal/helper/builtinplugins/registry.go:58-88. Auth: approle, cert, jwt/oidc, kubernetes, userpass. Secrets engines: kv, pki, transit, ssh, totp, kubernetes, rabbitmq, database. Database plugins: mysql, postgresql, cassandra, influxdb, valkey/redis. Audit devices: file, http, socket, syslog (commands.go:126-131). External plugins run as separate gRPC processes via sdk/plugin and go-plugin (website/content/docs/internals/limits.mdx:244-260). Separate importable Go modules: api/ (client plus api/auth/* helpers) and sdk/ (framework, logical, physical, helpers). Non-Go trees: ui/ (Ember 4.12, pnpm; ui/package.json:96,133,228) and website/ (Docusaurus 3). Layout is described in website/content/community/contributing/code-organization.mdx, which is partly stale (see risks).
code.packaging_and_release: Release is a manually dispatched 'Prepare release' workflow that builds a draft GitHub release; a maintainer reviews and publishes it, which triggers the image and package-repo workflows (.github/workflows/release.yml:1-19,350-362; release-images.yml:3-6; release-packages.yml:3-6). Artifacts per version: `bao` archives for 19 OS/arch targets (linux amd64/arm64/armv6/ppc64le/riscv64/s390x, darwin amd64/arm64, freebsd/netbsd/openbsd amd64/arm64/armv6, windows amd64/arm64; release.yml:119-139), built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and -tags=ui (release.yml:116; scripts/release/build.sh:31). Archives are openbao_<ver>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz (.zip on Windows) containing LICENSE, README.md and CHANGELOG.md (scripts/release/archive.sh:14-31). Also deb/rpm for each Linux arch plus Arch Linux packages for amd64/arm64 via nFPM (release.yml:185-200; .release/nfpm.yaml); SPDX-JSON SBOMs per artifact via Syft (release.yml:206-214); a distribution source tarball with vendored Go modules and license reports (release.yml:262-311). Integrity: every artifact gets a detached GPG signature (.gpgsig) and a keyless cosign bundle (.sigstore.json), each verified at creation, with the cosign identity restricted to release.yml on main or release/* for the main repo (scripts/release/sign.sh:17-61); checksums.txt (SHA-256) is signed with both (scripts/release/checksums.sh:13-57); deb/rpm are also GPG-signed by nFPM (.release/nfpm.yaml:50-55); verification steps are documented (website/content/docs/install.mdx:197-262). No SLSA or GitHub build-provenance attestation step exists (no 'attest|slsa|provenance' match under .github). Container images: Alpine (openbao/openbao), UBI (openbao-ubi) and distroless (openbao-distroless), multi-arch, pushed to ghcr.io, quay.io and docker.io, cosign-signed by digest, with timestamps rewritten from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (Dockerfile:12-21,61,114; release-images.yml:54-95,168-169,197-206). apt/rpm repositories are synced to S3 behind pkgs.openbao.org (release-packages.yml:25-137). Nightlies use the same workflow from openbao/openbao-nightly (release.yml:31-37). GitHub Actions are pinned by commit SHA. Linux package extras: hardened systemd unit (.release/linux/package/usr/lib/systemd/system/openbao.service:11-29) and a default config using pebbledb plus a TLS listener (.release/linux/package/etc/openbao/openbao.hcl:6-21).
code.tests_and_ci: Go: standard testing + testify (go.mod:121) run through gotestsum (tools/go.mod:14; .github/workflows/test-go.yml:185-196). About 595 *_test.go files repo-wide (76 under sdk/, 18 under api/, the rest mainly under internal/). Acceptance tests are gated by BAO_ACC=1 (Makefile:71-77). UI: QUnit via Ember (ui/package.json:28,164), about 296 test files under ui/tests. 18 workflow files in .github/workflows: ci.yml (Go tests split into 16 partitions plus a binary-test runner with the `deadlock` tag, and a separate -race run; ci.yml:51-90, via reusable test-go.yml); code-checker.yml (golangci-lint v2.13.1 for root/sdk/api, Semgrep 1.171.0 with Go rules from tools/semgrep/ci, go mod tidy and sync-deps diff checks, protobuf regeneration diff check; the EL8 build check is disabled with `if: false`; code-checker.yml:21-132); codeql.yml (CodeQL for Go on push/PR and weekly); scorecard.yml (OpenSSF Scorecard weekly, results published); ui-ci.yml (Ember tests with Chrome); docs-ci.yml and docs-deploy.yml (Docusaurus build/lint, GitHub Pages deploy); changelog-checker.yml (requires changelog/<PR>.txt); verify-commits.yml (maintainer commits must be signature-verified); sync-deps.yaml; go-dependency-submission.yml; mirror.yml (pushes to Codeberg); publiccodeyml-check.yml; test-acc-dockeronly-nightly.yml (workflow_dispatch only; it calls ./.github/workflows/test-run-acc-tests-for-path.yml, which is not in the tree); and release.yml, release-images.yml, release-packages.yml. dependabot.yml covers docker, github-actions, gomod (/ and /tools) and npm for /website only. CI tests run on ubuntu-latest amd64 only (ci.yml:65-67). No secret-scanning or dependency-vulnerability job in CI; govulncheck exists only as the manual `make vulncheck` (Makefile:233-237). Local hooks are copied by `make prep` (Makefile:131-133): .hooks/pre-commit runs UI lint-staged and gofmt on staged Go files only (.hooks/pre-commit:38-73); .hooks/pre-push enforces DCO Signed-off-by (.hooks/pre-push:22-30).
code.dependencies: Go modules (direct requires / indirect): go.mod (root, go 1.27.0) 120 / 191 (go.mod:26-147,149-341); api/go.mod (go 1.25.0) 13 / 12; sdk/go.mod (go 1.27.0) 44 / 50; tools/go.mod 0 direct and 10 `tool` directives (golangci-lint, misspell, go-licenses, changelog-build, zlint, govulncheck, protoc-gen-go-grpc, protoc-gen-go, gotestsum, gofumpt; tools/go.mod:5-16) with 247 indirect; api/auth/{approle,jwt,kubernetes,ldap,userpass}/go.mod 1 direct each (api/v2; e.g. api/auth/approle/go.mod:7); internal/helper/stubbolt/go.mod has none (a local stub replacing github.com/boltdb/bolt, go.mod:24). The root module pulls HashiCorp libraries (raft, go-plugin, cap), Kubernetes and Google client libraries directly (go.mod:46,75,138,141-143) and Azure/AWS SDKs indirectly (go.mod:155-160,173-187). replace directives point api, sdk and api/auth/* at local paths (go.mod:14-24). The source tarball ships license reports generated by go-licenses and the pnpm license tooling (release.yml:262-292).
code.security_policy: No SECURITY.md in this checkout (root and .github/ checked). Disclosure is by private mail to openbao-security@lists.openssf.org (README.md:5-8; CONTRIBUTING.md:3-5; .github/security-insights.yml:152-159). The SECURITY.md it points to lives in the org-level openbao/.github repo (CONTRIBUTING.md:141-142; website/content/community/policies/cve.mdx:26-27) and was not opened. CVE process: 7 days to confirm, 90-day patch window, embargoed fixes limited to security-list members (website/content/community/policies/cve.mdx:12-19,50-76). Threat model: website/content/docs/internals/security.mdx:18-97. GHSA advisory IDs are cited throughout CHANGELOG.md (41 lines). security-insights.yml says the project's security self-assessment 'has not yet been completed' (.github/security-insights.yml:192-195).

claim_checks.claim: Dynamic Secrets 'such as AWS or SQL databases' - OpenBao generates an AWS keypair on demand (README.md:53-57)
claim_checks.evidence: The code differs from the README. The built-in registry has database plugins (mysql, postgresql, cassandra, influxdb, redis/valkey) plus kubernetes, rabbitmq, ssh, pki, totp, transit and kv engines, but no AWS secrets engine (internal/helper/builtinplugins/registry.go:66-88). The plugin policy says cloud-vendor engines including secrets-aws were moved out of the binary (website/content/community/policies/plugins.mdx:24-28,171), and the docs intro already uses a Kubernetes example instead (website/content/docs/what-is-openbao.mdx:46-49). SQL dynamic credentials are real; AWS would need an external plugin, which I did not inspect.

claim_checks.claim: OpenBao encrypts secrets before writing them to persistent storage (README.md:47-51)
claim_checks.evidence: The encryption barrier builds an AES-GCM AEAD (aes.NewCipher + cipher.NewGCMWithRandomNonce) in internal/vault/barrier/aes_gcm.go:999-1013, generates a 32-byte (256-bit) key at :340-344 and accepts 16-32 byte keys (:347-350). The docs describe the same design (website/content/docs/internals/security.mdx:120-129).

claim_checks.claim: 'OpenBao can write to disk, PostgreSQL, and more' (README.md:50-51)
claim_checks.evidence: Registered storage backends are inmem_ha, inmem, raft, postgresql and pebbledb (internal/command/commands.go:145-151; internal/physical/postgresql/postgresql.go). Caveat: the older `file` backend was removed in 2.7.0 (website/content/community/release-notes/2-7-0.mdx:77; CHANGELOG.md:15), so 'disk' now means raft or pebbledb.

claim_checks.claim: All secrets have leases that are revoked automatically; single secrets or trees can be revoked and renewed (README.md:64-72)
claim_checks.evidence: ExpirationManager implements Register (internal/vault/expiration.go:1483), Renew (:1259), Revoke (:957), RevokePrefix (:1139) and RevokeByToken (:1150).

claim_checks.claim: Data Encryption: encrypt and decrypt data without storing it (README.md:59-62)
claim_checks.evidence: The transit secrets engine is built in (internal/helper/builtinplugins/registry.go:87; internal/builtin/logical/transit/backend.go).

Audit device factories file, http, socket and syslog are registered (internal/command/commands.go:126-131). The docs say most strings in audit entries are hashed with a salted HMAC-SHA256 so secrets are not logged in plaintext (website/content/docs/audit/index.mdx:68).

claim_checks.claim: The repository publishes two libraries: api/v2 and sdk/v2 (README.md:131-132)
claim_checks.evidence: Both modules exist (api/go.mod:1; sdk/go.mod:1). Five more api/auth/* modules (approle, jwt, kubernetes, ldap, userpass) have their own go.mod and are tagged by `make tag-api` (api/auth/*/go.mod; Makefile:284-299), so more than two libraries are published.

claim_checks.claim: The Go toolchain used in CI and releases is pinned at .go-version (README.md:88-90)
claim_checks.evidence: .go-version:1 is 1.27.1. The in-repo set-up-go action reads it (.github/actions/set-up-go/action.yml:25-30) and release.yml:145-146 and ci.yml:38-39 use that action. go.mod:12 separately says `go 1.27.0`.

claim_checks.claim: Security issues go privately to openbao-security@lists.openssf.org (README.md:5-8)
claim_checks.evidence: Consistent with .github/security-insights.yml:152-159 and website/content/community/policies/cve.mdx:26. There is no SECURITY.md in this checkout; the referenced policy file is in the org-level .github repo (CONTRIBUTING.md:141), which I did not open.

claim_checks.claim: Scope for the stated needs: the README presents OpenBao as a secrets manager (manage, store, distribute) and makes no claim about scanning repositories for leaked secrets or verifying found credentials (README.md:33-36)
claim_checks.evidence: Matches the code. A repo-wide case-insensitive search for gitleaks, trufflehog, detect-secrets, git-secrets, secretlint, ggshield, gitguardian, 'secret scanning/scanner/detection' and 'vault radar' returned no matches. The repo's own pre-commit hook runs only UI lint-staged and gofmt (.hooks/pre-commit:38-73). CI scanners are golangci-lint, Semgrep, CodeQL and Scorecard (.github/workflows/code-checker.yml:21-67; codeql.yml; scorecard.yml). Semgrep rule files in tools/semgrep/ci/ are named for Go correctness checks (contents not opened). The only 'scan' feature is a recursive-list API operation (website/content/community/rfcs/scan-operation.mdx:11).

benchmarks.metric: latency mean / p95 / p99 in ms, request count

benchmarks.what: KV v1 write latency, same setup as the read benchmark
benchmarks.metric: latency mean / p95 / p99 in ms, request count

benchmarks.value: over 300k mounts and 20k namespaces (benchmarks are in the separate benchmark-openbao repo, not opened)

risks: Scope mismatch with the stated needs: OpenBao is a secrets manager and cannot serve as the main secret scanner or the credential-verification complement. It has no scanning or verification feature, and the repo uses no such tool (repo-wide search for common scanners found nothing; .hooks/pre-commit:38-73 runs only UI lint and gofmt; CI scanners are golangci-lint, Semgrep, CodeQL and Scorecard, .github/workflows/code-checker.yml:21-67). Using it also means running, initializing and unsealing a server (website/content/docs/commands/server.mdx:10-14); -dev mode is in-memory and not for production (server.mdx:103-105).

Frequent security fixes and a thin support window: v2.7.1 (2026-10-01) carries 6 security fixes (CHANGELOG.md:1-11) and v2.7.0 (2026-09-23) carries 9 (CHANGELOG.md:25-38); 41 CHANGELOG lines cite GHSA advisories. The support policy guarantees only the latest release ('The latest release does not EoL'), with releases 'roughly every month pending maintainer availability' (website/content/community/policies/support.mdx:17).

Credentials land on disk by default: the CLI token helper writes the token in plaintext to ~/.vault-token (mode 0600) or $BAO_TOKEN_PATH (internal/command/token/helper_internal.go:27-35,67; website/content/docs/commands/index.mdx:270-272); dev mode persists the dev root token to that helper unless -dev-no-store-token is given (server.mdx:123-125); the Agent file sink writes tokens at default mode 0640 (website/content/docs/agent-and-proxy/autoauth/sinks/file.mdx:16-18). If BAO_TOKEN_PATH or a sink path points inside a working tree, nothing in OpenBao prevents committing it.

Docs and README drift from the code (prefer the code): the README names AWS dynamic secrets, but no AWS engine is built in (registry.go:66-88); install.mdx:86-87 says the binary package is a zip, but non-Windows archives are .tar.gz (scripts/release/archive.sh:28-31); code-organization.mdx:149-151 says Raft is the only production storage backend, but commands.go:145-151 registers raft, postgresql and pebbledb; code-organization.mdx:87-90 says the SDK is versioned at major 0, but sdk/go.mod:1 is sdk/v2; commands/index.mdx:279-280 says all environment variables are logged at startup, but server.go:677-700 logs only proxy variables, with credentials redacted; the Helm doc describes a file storage backend (website/content/docs/platform/k8s/helm/index.mdx:61-63) that 2.7.0 removed (2-7-0.mdx:77).

Build-from-source portability: building needs Go 1.27.x (go.mod:12; .go-version:1). The EL8 Go-version build check is disabled and such platforms are left to unreleased v2.6.x patches (.github/workflows/code-checker.yml:80-84). Go 1.27 already forced a behavior change: PKI no longer accepts FQDNs ending in '.' (website/content/community/release-notes/2-7-0.mdx:85).

Release and CI gaps: artifacts have SHA-256 checksums, GPG and cosign signatures and SPDX SBOMs, but no build-provenance attestation step (no 'attest|slsa|provenance' match under .github). Tests run only on linux/amd64 (ci.yml:65-67) while darwin, windows and BSD binaries are cross-compiled on Ubuntu (release.yml:104,116-139). There is no govulncheck/OSV job in CI (only manual `make vulncheck`, Makefile:233-237). test-acc-dockeronly-nightly.yml:13,22 calls a reusable workflow that is not in the tree. Dependabot does not list /ui (dependabot.yml:69-72 covers only /website) although the UI ships inside release binaries (-tags=ui, scripts/release/build.sh:31).

API and maturity caveats: the HTTP API docs say backwards compatibility is not yet promised even with the v1 prefix (website/content/docs/api/index.mdx:16-23); importing the root Go module is unsupported (README.md:134-143); the security self-assessment is not completed (.github/security-insights.yml:192-195); OSPS-BR-01.01 (CI input sanitisation) has no recorded status (website/content/community/policies/osps-baseline.mdx:19,64-66). Governance is a 6-member TSC drawn from 6 organizations (CONTRIBUTING.md:80-89) with 4 org-level maintainers (MAINTAINERS.md:12-19).

Licensing and contribution rules: LICENSE is MPL-2.0 under a 'Copyright (c) 2015 HashiCorp, Inc.' header (LICENSE:1-3). The project bars copying from HashiCorp's source-available (BSL) code and requires clean-room parity work (CONTRIBUTING.md:22-29), and inbound code must be MPL-2.0 with a DCO sign-off (CHARTER.md:106-108). It asks contributors to disable generative AI agents, naming Claude Code (CONTRIBUTING.md:38-54). The UI depends on @hashicorp design-system packages (ui/package.json:222-224) whose licenses I did not examine.

Docs say the package is a zip (install.mdx:86-87), but non-Windows archives are .tar.gz (scripts/release/archive.sh:28-31).
